title: Meet Java Checkpoint
intro: You have met the JVM, written a class with a main method, printed text and read your first error messages. Eleven rounds, one from every idea in this module. Get them right first time to earn three stars!

rounds.prompt: Run this program. What appears on the screen?
rounds.explain: `println` prints whatever is inside the double quotes. The quotes mark where the text starts and ends, so they are not printed themselves.

rounds.prompt: Where does the JVM start running a Java program?
options: At the first line of the file
rounds.explain: The JVM looks for a method named `main` and begins there. Misspell it and the program compiles but never starts, because nothing tells the JVM where to begin.

rounds.prompt: This line will not compile. Pick the fix.
options: Put the whole line in curly braces
rounds.explain: Every Java instruction ends with a semicolon. Without it `javac` keeps reading onto the next line and reports `';' expected`.

rounds.prompt: Your file contains `public class Player`. What must the file be named?
rounds.explain: The file name must match the public class exactly, capital letters included. `.class` is the bytecode file that `javac` writes for you, not the one you write.

rounds.prompt: Careful: one of these does not start a new line. What is the output?
rounds.explain: `print` stays on the same line, so `Lab` continues straight after `Pocket` with no space. Only the `println` ends the line.

options: Nothing: you cannot join a number to text
rounds.explain: `+` joins the pieces together, and Java turns the number 10 into the character `1` followed by `0` so it can be part of the text.

rounds.prompt: Which escape sequence prints a double quote?
rounds.explain: `\n` is a new line, `\t` is a tab and `\\` is a single backslash. `\"` prints a double quote without ending the text.

rounds.prompt: This program compiles and prints nothing at all. Why?
options: The `//` turned the instruction into a comment, so Java ignores it
`println` cannot be used twice in one program
rounds.explain: Anything after `//` is a note for humans. Commenting out a line switches it off without deleting it, which is a handy way to test what a line was doing.

rounds.prompt: Your program prints two lines and then shows an error. What kind of error is it?
options: A runtime error: it compiled, started, then broke
A compile error: `javac` refused to translate it
Both a compile and a runtime error
Not an error: programs always print two lines first
rounds.explain: Output appearing proves the code compiled and the JVM started it, so whatever went wrong happened while the program was running.

rounds.prompt: Match each piece of Java to what it does.

pairs.right: Checks your code and makes bytecode
Prints, then moves to a new line
Marks the end of an instruction

rounds.explain: These six cover the whole module: the two steps that run your code, the starting point, printing, and the two bits of punctuation you will type most often.

rounds.prompt: Build the smallest working program: open the class, open main, print a greeting, then close both.
rounds.explain: The class is the outer box and `main` is the inner one, so the instruction sits inside both and the braces close in the opposite order to how they opened: method first, then class.
